# QS-CFW-6476-89 — Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (52100)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-6476-89

Scope
- This quality specification applies to forging, heat treat, machining, and final inspection of bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) manufactured at Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria for hardness, bore tolerance, and maximum forging weight for production lots and for material released to downstream processing.

Requirements table
| Item | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| Material | 52100 bearing steel per procurement | Conforming certificate required |
| Hardness | The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 29-32 HRC. | All rings must measure within range on final inspection |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is ±0.04 mm. | Measured values outside tolerance = nonconformance |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 119.0 kg. | Forgings exceeding weight are rejected at incoming inspection |

Inspection method
- Hardness: Locate and record hardness at the specified final-inspection locations using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Report individual readings and the lot-level summary. Verify that the hardness range for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 29-32 HRC.
- Dimensional: Inspect bore diameter with calibrated bore gauge or coordinate measuring machine. Report nominal and measured values, and confirm compliance with the bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is ±0.04 mm.
- Weight: Verify forging weight on calibrated scale at incoming inspection and record in material traceability record. Confirm the maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 119.0 kg.

Nonconformance handling
- Parts failing any listed requirement shall be segregated, tagged, and documented on a nonconformance report. Root cause analysis and containment actions are required prior to disposition. Disposition options include rework if the corrective action can demonstrably restore compliance to the specified requirements, or scrap if restoration is not possible. All dispositions must be recorded with traceability to the affected lot and inspection records.
